issue.title: event-link-times 200-link Live Preview 25 ms wall-clock assertion flakes under full npm test load
issue.description:
Proposed by bob-cli-kj.6 (note #2, PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP) and triaged by the bob-cli-kj
land agent. Not caused by bob-cli-kj. The test came from 8ce2feb ("feat(ledger-tools):
event link time pills with gcal now-on-timeline fix"), and kj.6 only touched
block-id-prompt.

## What fails

`scripts/test-ledger-tools-event-link-times.cjs:1069`,
`perf — one build over a 200-link ledger stays under 25 ms`, failed in a full
bob-plugins `npm test` on athena (load ~18): **427.6 ms against 25 ms**. The rest of
that file's assertions passed.

## Root cause (from the source)

After one warm build, the test times a single
`plugin.buildEventLinkTimeDecorations(view)` call with `process.hrtime.bigint()`, which
is wall clock, and asserts `ms < 25`. Under the parallel `node --test` run of about 400
files, scheduler preemption and suite contention count as algorithm time. This is the
same single-sample wall-clock pattern as bob-cli-io (frees-marks), bob-cli-ju
(off-clock link chips), and bob-cli-ki (keep-moving marks surface), on a different test
node.

## Isolation control

bob-cli-kj.land, bob-plugins master 70408bf: `node --test
scripts/test-ledger-tools-event-link-times.cjs` passed 23/23 three times in a row.

## Fix

Keep the deterministic assertion that all 200 links pill, and keep a meaningful
regression gate: for example, use the CPU-time minimum of several samples, or a
counted-work assertion. Do not just raise the 25 ms threshold. Prefer the same
measurement repair the sibling beads adopt, so the four nodes stay consistent.

task_type_fields.evidence: 1 failure in 2 reported full-suite runs (bob-cli-kj.6, athena load ~18: 427.6 ms vs 25 ms); 3/3 isolated passes (23/23) by bob-cli-kj.land on 70408bf. Parallel-suite only; never seen serially.
